issues.code_location: BaseFeeMarket.computeBaseFee() - interface method declaration, no implementation body
issues.description: The file only declares abstract Wei computeBaseFee(blockNumber, parentBaseFee, parentBlockGasUsed, targetGasUsed) with no formula. It does not implement the EIP-1559 base-fee update rules (parent_gas_target comparison, BASE_FEE_MAX_CHANGE_DENOMINATOR=8 division, max(...,1) floor on increase, subtraction on decrease) nor enforcement of the result.
issues.potential_impact: Without a concrete verified formula, nodes using this interface alone cannot enforce correct baseFee; incorrect or missing calculation leads to consensus split, invalid blocks accepted/rejected, and fee-market manipulation.
issues.spec_reference: elif parent_gas_used > parent_gas_target: gas_used_delta = parent_gas_used - parent_gas_target base_fee_per_gas_delta = max(parent_base_fee_per_gas * gas_used_delta // parent_gas_target // BASE_FEE_MAX_CHANGE_DENOMINATOR, 1) expected_base_fee_per_gas = parent_base_fee_per_gas + base_fee_per_gas_delta
issues.suggestion: Provide/verify concrete implementation (e.g. LondonFeeMarket) that exactly implements parent_gas_target logic, denominator 8, increase floor of 1 wei, and decrease without floor, with integer division round-down and overflow-safe Uint/Wei arithmetic.

issues.description: No validation logic enforces fork initialization: expected_base_fee_per_gas = INITIAL_BASE_FEE on INITIAL_FORK_BLOCK_NUMBER and adjusted parent_gas_target/parent_gas_limit handling to avoid halving target. ValidationMode enums are defined but never asserted against header.base_fee_per_gas in this file.
issues.potential_impact: Missing/incorrect fork-block handling causes all fork-block and early post-fork blocks to be validated against wrong expected fee, causing chain split at upgrade or allowing miners to set arbitrary initial base fee.
issues.suggestion: Implement header validation that returns INITIAL_BASE_FEE (1000000000) when block.number == fork block, uses parent_gas_target = parent.gas_limit (not divided) on fork block, and otherwise asserts expected_base_fee_per_gas == block.base_fee_per_gas.

issues.code_location: BaseFeeMarket.java - entire file, no gas-limit validation logic; targetGasUsed() helper only
issues.description: Only default targetGasUsed() = gasLimit/slackCoefficient is present. Missing consensus checks: block.gas_used <= block.gas_limit, gas_limit delta < parent_gas_limit/1024 in both directions, and block.gas_limit >= 5000. gasLimitValidationMode() is abstract with no enforcement.
issues.potential_impact: Without gas-limit bounds, malicious miners could produce oversized blocks or drift gas limit arbitrarily, causing DoS, processing overload, and consensus divergence from clients enforcing EIP-1559 limits.
issues.spec_reference: assert block.gas_limit < parent_gas_limit + parent_gas_limit // 1024, 'invalid block: gas limit increased too much'
issues.suggestion: Add concrete block-header validation enforcing gas_used <= gas_limit, gas_limit within parent +/- parent//1024, and gas_limit >= 5000, and wire gasLimitValidationMode to enforce it after fork.

verification.matched_excerpt: assert block.gas_limit < parent_gas_limit + parent_gas_limit // 1024, 'invalid block: gas limit increased too much'

issues.description: File contains no check that transaction.max_fee_per_gas >= block.base_fee_per_gas, no max_fee >= max_priority_fee check, no 2**256 range checks, and no legacy/access-list mapping to effective pricing. Fee-cap validation is entirely absent.
issues.potential_impact: Transactions paying below base fee could be included, violating protocol validity, enabling fee evasion and consensus split between this client and spec-compliant clients.
issues.suggestion: Implement transaction includability check rejecting any FeeMarketTransaction with max_fee_per_gas < base_fee_per_gas, enforcing max_fee >= max_priority_fee and <2**256, and for legacy tx enforcing gas_price >= base_fee.

issues.description: Missing EIP-1559 pricing core: priority_fee_per_gas = min(max_priority_fee, max_fee - base_fee) and effective_gas_price = priority_fee + base_fee. Interface exposes no method to compute or propagate effective price to execution/GASPRICE.
issues.potential_impact: Incorrect priority capping overcharges sender, overpays miner, or undercharges base fee; breaks GASPRICE semantics and causes state-root/balance divergence and consensus failure.
issues.suggestion: Implement getEffectiveGasPrice(max_fee, max_priority_fee, base_fee) with min-capping, use it for upfront gas deduction, refund (gas_left * effective_price), and expose via FeeMarket for TransactionEnvironment and GASPRICE opcode.

issues.code_location: BaseFeeMarket.java - no balance update / burn logic
issues.description: File has no logic for burning base fee or crediting miner only priority_fee * gas_used. No account balance updates, no refund using effective price, and no GASPRICE opcode requirement. Cannot verify that base fee is destroyed and miner does not receive it.
issues.potential_impact: If base fee is credited to miner instead of burned, it enables miner manipulation of base fee for profit, breaks ETH supply/burn invariant, and diverges from spec chain state.
issues.suggestion: Ensure transaction execution charges gas_used * effective_gas_price to sender, credits miner only gas_used * priority_fee_per_gas, burns gas_used * base_fee (sends to no one), and make GASPRICE (0x3a) return effective_gas_price.

summary: BaseFeeMarket.java is only an interface with abstract methods (computeBaseFee, validation modes) and one helper targetGasUsed; it contains no consensus-critical logic for base-fee calculation, header/fee validation, priority-fee capping, burn, or GASPRICE. Compliance cannot be established from this file alone and must be verified in concrete FeeMarket implementations.
